sections.h2: What should a Voorhees homeowner know before selling fast?
sections.html:
Selling fast in Voorhees depends on three things: whether the township will sign off on the house, how much the state collects at closing, and how soon a buyer can fund. Voorhees Township is a Camden County suburb of Philadelphia, with detached houses, townhouses and apartments side by side.

Most owners compare a regular listing with a cash buyer who takes the house with its flaws. Both meet the same township and state steps. The gap is how long you carry the house and how much you spend on repairs beforehand.

sections.h2: Where is Voorhees and what shapes its housing market?
sections.html:
Voorhees covers 11.47 square miles of land in western Camden County and was incorporated in 1899 out of Waterford Township. Census counts jumped from 1,450 in 1940 to 12,919 in 1980 and 24,559 in 1990, which is when most of the housing stock went up. The 2020 census counted 31,069 residents, and the Census Bureau estimates 31,571 for July 1, 2025.

The township borders Cherry Hill, Gibbsboro, Berlin Township, Lindenwold, Somerdale and Lawnside in Camden County, plus Evesham Township in Burlington County. Echelon, the census-designated place in the western part of town, held 11,896 people in 2020. Older names such as Kresson, Kirkwood, Glendale and Osage still show up in addresses and school names.

  • Route 73 (Berlin-Kresson Road) is the only major highway that runs through Voorhees.
  • Interstate 295 and Route 70 reach Philadelphia by way of Cherry Hill, and Exit 32 of I-295 is partly signed for Voorhees.
  • The Ashland station of the PATCO Speedline sits inside the township, and NJ Transit runs the 403 bus to Philadelphia.

Of the 119.81 miles of road in the township, 96.90 miles are municipal, 20.50 are county and 2.41 belong to the state, so most street repairs and plowing questions go to the township. Virtua Voorhees Hospital on Route 73 opened in May 2011 on a 40-acre site. The township offices sit at Voorhees Town Center, the former Echelon Mall, and the Glendale Methodist Episcopal Church of 1855 is on the National Register of Historic Places. New Jersey American Water, the state's largest water utility, was long headquartered here, and the Flyers Training Center draws professional hockey players to the area.

Only 62.0% of homes are owner-occupied, which is low for a New Jersey suburb and points to a sizable stock of condominiums, townhouses and rentals next to the detached houses. If you own a townhouse or condo, ask your association what documents it issues for a sale.

Voorhees Township Public Schools teach pre-kindergarten through eighth grade. The district listed five schools in the 2019-20 school year: Hamilton, Kresson, Osage and Signal Hill elementary schools, and Voorhees Middle School with 1,018 students. High school students attend Eastern Camden County Regional High School, which the township shares with Berlin Borough and Gibbsboro.

Edward T. Hamilton Elementary was named a National Blue Ribbon School in 2003-2004. The Camden County Library's largest branch, the M. Allan Vogelson Regional Branch, is in Voorhees. Voorhees has four elementary schools, so find out which one your street feeds before you list.

sections.h2: What else do Voorhees buyers look at besides the house?
sections.html:
Buyers compare more than square footage. Voorhees has a 368-bed hospital, Virtua Voorhees, on Route 73, and the largest branch of the Camden County Library at the M. Allan Vogelson Regional Branch, open since 1969. Two private schools, Kellman Brown Academy (a Jewish day school for ages 3 through grade 8) and the Naudain Academy Montessori program, add options beyond the public K-8 district.

The Flyers Training Center, expanded in 2018, and a community park with a running track, playground, gazebo and dog areas round out the amenities. Saddlehill Vineyard and Winery opened in 2021 on the former Stafford Farm. Mention the ones near your street in the listing.

sections.h2: What does the township require before a Voorhees house changes hands?
sections.html:
The township construction office handles certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy, so call it first. Ask whether a change of owner needs a resale certificate, what the inspection covers, and how long the certificate lasts before closing.

Unpermitted work is the usual snag. A finished basement, deck or converted garage built without a permit can hold up the certificate until the permit is closed or the work removed, so pull your permit history before you sign a contract.

  • One- and two-family homes need smoke alarms with 10-year sealed batteries before a sale (N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19).
  • That rule leaves hardwired and low-voltage alarm systems and carbon monoxide alarms alone.
  • Ask the construction office for its current checklist, inspection fee and scheduling window.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when you sell in Voorhees?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state's Realty Transfer Fee, set per $500 of price by bracket. For sales over $350,000 the $200,000 to $550,000 bracket carries $4.80 per $500, and Voorhees's Census median of $429,700 sits inside it. Above $1 million the buyer owes an extra 1% and the seller a graduated fee.

Every owner on the deed signs a GIT/REP form. Staying in New Jersey means GIT/REP-3 and no prepayment. Moving out of state can mean prepaying the state either 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain. A main home that you owned and lived in for two of the last five years may qualify for the federal gain exclusion.

Have your closing attorney file the transfer fee affidavit with the deed. The county clerk can refuse a deed that arrives incomplete.

sections.h2: How do property tax assessments and appeals work in Voorhees?
sections.html:
Disputes over a Voorhees assessment go to the Camden County Board of Taxation, 509 Lakeland Road in Blackwood, phone 856-225-5238. Camden County keeps the regular calendar: April 1, or May 1 after a municipal revaluation. A property valued above $1,000,000 can go straight to Tax Court.

The board weighs comparable sales more than your opinion of fair value, and an appeal does little for a seller about to close. A buyer or heir who keeps the house might benefit. Owners of a main home may qualify for the state's Homestead Benefit or Senior Freeze, and the township handles local deductions for seniors, disabled owners and veterans.

sections.h2: How does Voorhees weather affect a house for sale?
sections.html:
Voorhees sits in a transition zone between humid continental and humid subtropical climates. Average July highs reach 87 degrees, record lows have dropped to minus 13, and the year brings about 41 inches of precipitation across roughly 117 wet days and nearly 23 inches of snow.

That mix tests roofs, gutters, sump pumps and heating systems. Buyers and inspectors look at those items first, so a house with a recent roof or serviced boiler needs fewer repair credits. A cash buyer pricing the house as-is will weigh the same items.

  • Roof and gutters: ask for the install year and any warranty paperwork.
  • Basement: note any past water, and what was done about it.
  • Heating and cooling: gather service records for the last few seasons.

faqs.q: How soon could a Voorhees house sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale often closes within a few weeks. A listed sale runs longer because of showings, the buyer's loan and any township review, so ask the construction office how long its resale inspection takes.

faqs.q: Does Voorhees need an occupancy certificate for a sale?
faqs.a: Call the township construction office, which issues the certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy used when a house changes owners. State law separately calls for 10-year sealed-battery smoke alarms in one- and two-family homes.

faqs.q: Who covers the transfer fee on a Voorhees sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it when the deed is recorded. The buyer's extra 1% starts at $1 million, far above the $429,700 Census median for Voorhees homes.

faqs.q: What is the last day to contest a Voorhees assessment?
faqs.a: April 1 in Camden County, or May 1 after a revaluation. Use Form A-1 and call the Camden County Board of Taxation in Blackwood at 856-225-5238.

faqs.q: Will open permits stop a Voorhees sale?
faqs.a: They can slow the township's sign-off. Have the construction office review your permit history, then close the permits or agree in writing with the buyer on who repairs what and by when.
